answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent refuses to reopen price, so renewing or negotiating harder won't meet the objective and c4 already tells us benchmarking pressure alone didn't make the incumbent move this cycle. The line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract expires in 14 days, so switching the whole primary at once is too dangerous; c1 shows incumbency protects stability, and c3 shows a second source was the move that actually got us through a shortage. So the highest-expected-value action is a guarded switch: qualify the low-cost vendor on a small share first (consistent with c2), keep the incumbent in place during the transition to protect delivery, and only rotate volume to the new vendor as deliveries prove out. c6 is not a fit right now because multi-year commitment with an unwilling incumbent won't unlock the 18% cut.
